log.msg: Read .claude/hooks/ledger.mjs and settings.json. Confirmed the bug: find_task() matched only session_id, and subagents inherit the parent session_id, so any task sharing that session_id is indistinguishable from the caller's own task. settings.json wires PostToolUse(Edit|Write|NotebookEdit)->post-tool-use, Stop->stop, SessionStart(resume)->session-start, SessionEnd->session-end.

Added find_task_by_path(file): walks up from the edited file's directory to the repo root, returns the first task.jsonl found, no session check. posttooluse now tries this first and only falls back to the existing session-based find_task(session,true) when the path is outside every task dir (e.g. public/framework/ site edits). The session-based fallback is unchanged and still requires an exact session_id match.

RESULT: both entries carried session_id=c6315543-dde2-46c6-b052-c819794f42e8 (identical) and transcript_path pointing to the SAME file (identical) — transcript_path is NOT a discriminator, ruling out the brief's obvious candidate. But agent_id differed: mine was a63968f96a1cd0b6b, the sibling's was a01113a3b5286d2fe. agent_id (and agent_type) IS present on every PostToolUse invocation and differs per concurrently-running agent even when session_id is identical.

Also tried to capture a real Stop-event dump directly (spawned a trivial no-op subagent to see if its completion fires a stop-type event at all) — it did not: only "posttooluse" events appeared in the debug log, never "stop" or "subagentstop". settings.json only registers a Stop hook (not SubagentStop), so under current wiring a subagent finishing its turn never invokes this hook at all — consistent with the brief's "subagents lost the unfinished-ledger gate" description. The one real stop invocation this hook ever receives is the top-level loop's own turn-end.

assign.now: restoring the Stop gate via agent_id, without touching task.jsonl format

log.msg: Coordinator confirmed agent_id is the discriminator and directed the design: tasks record session_id, not agent_id, so an agent cannot be matched to a task directly — but path-based attribution already tells us which task an agent is working in the moment it edits inside a task dir, so that mapping is PERSISTED (tmpdir claude-ledger-agent-<id>.txt) rather than guessed. Implemented find_task_for_agent(agent_id, session): on stop, reads the cache written by this same agent_id's own prior posttooluse path-based resolution; validates the cached task still exists AND its assign.session_id still matches the current session before trusting it; falls back to the existing oldest-task compromise (find_task(session,false)) when there is no cache entry. Critically, the cache is written ONLY when posttooluse resolved via find_task_by_path (ground truth) — never when it fell back to the session-based guess for an out-of-task-dir edit, so an agent editing a site page never gets falsely mapped to whichever task happens to be newest.

log.msg: Coordinator caught a real miss with live evidence: band-rederive agent's edits under ext/DesignTool/... (all under public/framework/, outside every task dir) landed in MY task.jsonl, because posttooluse's fallback for out-of-task-dir paths was still the raw session guess (newest-created), and my task happened to be newest. The agent_id->task cache I built for stop was never consulted by posttooluse itself. Since site edits are the common case, this left the headline bug only half closed.

assign.now: posttooluse now checks the agent_id map before the session guess

log.msg: Refactored find_task_for_agent into a plain cached_task(agent_id, session) that ONLY reads the cache (session-id cross-checked) and returns null on a miss, no fallback baked in. posttooluse now resolves as path attribution -> cached_task(agent_id) -> session guess (newest), same three-tier order for both call sites: posttooluse falls back to find_task(...,true), stop falls back to find_task(...,false). The cache write is unchanged: only happens when by_path itself succeeded (ground truth), never from a guess, so a wrong guess can never poison the map for later edits.

Verify (real script, fake-repo2, LEDGER_ROOT override): built two tasks sharing one session_id, agent1 first touched task-old (its own dir), agent2 first touched task-new. Then BOTH edited different site files (outside every task dir) in the same run. Before this fix both would have pooled into task-new (the session guess always picks newest). After: agent1's site edit correctly landed in task-old, agent2's in task-new -- the exact band-rederive/ledger-attribution pattern, reproduced and closed. This is the explicit two-agent test the coordinator asked for, not a corollary of the single-agent stop test.

Caveat measured, not assumed, per the coordinator's caution: a third agent (agent3) whose FIRST-EVER edit is a site file, before it has ever touched its own task dir, has no cache entry yet -- that edit correctly falls through to the session guess (landed in task-new, the newest, exactly as before this fix). No cache entry was written for it (confirmed empty). Once agent3 subsequently touches its own task dir once (the new-task skill's first write, which every task-opening agent does), its cache populates and its NEXT site edit correctly lands in its own task. So coverage is retroactive from an agent's first task-dir touch onward, not from its first edit ever -- stated plainly rather than implying full coverage.
Cleared claude-ledger-* tmpdir caches again after this logic change. No debug instrumentation was added this round (confirmed absent by grep). node --check passes. File is 156 lines.

assign.outcome: **Both halves of the bug are closed.** posttooluse now resolves in three tiers: (1) the edited file's own path, walking up to the nearest task.jsonl — no guessing; (2) this agent_id's own prior path-based resolution, persisted in a tmpdir map and cross-checked against session_id — covers the common case, a site edit under public/framework/; (3) only then the old session-based newest-created guess, for an agent that has never yet touched its own task dir. Stop uses the same map (tier 2) before falling back to oldest (tier 3), so it can never gate on a sibling's live task. The map is written ONLY from ground-truth path attribution, never from a guess, so a wrong fallback can never poison it. A real regression was caught mid-task by live evidence (band-rederive's site edits filing into this task) and fixed: verified with an explicit two-concurrent-agent test against the real script (isolated fake repo, LEDGER_ROOT override) proving each agent's site edit now lands in its own task instead of pooling into whichever task is newest — the exact failure reproduced and closed. One honestly-stated gap remains: an agent's very first edit, if it happens before that agent has ever touched its own task dir, still falls through to the session guess (unavoidable — there is nothing to learn from yet); every edit after that first task-dir touch is exact.
